key_insight: A minimax framework shows that, under standard OT stability assumptions, learning any valid transport map can be as statistically hard as learning the optimal transport map.
engineering_relevance: For diffusion, flow matching, and normalizing-flow generative systems, this sets fundamental sample-complexity limits and tells engineers when simpler non-OT targets may or may not yield real gains.
method: Formalize transport-map estimation as a minimax statistical problem
Derive sample-complexity lower bounds for any learned transport map or plan
Compare OT and non-OT transport targets under stability vs. instability assumptions
evidence_signal: The paper relies on theoretical minimax analysis and example constructions, rather than empirical benchmarking, to show both lower bounds and cases where non-OT maps can be learned more accurately.
watch_item: The strongest hardness result depends on standard but strong stability assumptions; if those assumptions fail, conclusions about equivalence to OT may not hold.
paper_title: The Fundamental Limits of Valid Transport Map Estimation
